solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Old court bible, originally only this size?

indicators.note: originally points to the start of the next word, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
CT is the abbreviation for court
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible
first letter of only

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether an old court Bible was always printed in such a small format.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition leans on the clue itself: the pieces spell a book size, so 'this size' is that size.
explanation.definitionFit: Octavo is a traditional book format, made by folding each printed sheet into eight leaves.

clue.text: First-class police force once set up court in Rome

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised from bottom to top, so the letters are read upwards

blocks.note: A1 means first-class, written with the letter I standing in for the digit
the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police until 2001

explanation.surface: An old-time police force sets up a court in Rome, like a historical anecdote.
explanation.definitionFit: The Curia was the senate house of ancient Rome, and today names the papal court and administration in Rome.

clue.text: Day church converted Austrian prince's estate

indicators.note: something converted has been changed into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A church used for daytime worship has been converted into an Austrian nobleman's property.
explanation.definitionFit: An archduke was a prince of the Austrian Habsburg house, and his territory was an archduchy.

clue.text: Old boy, recent monastic dedicatee

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
late in the sense of recently happened, as in 'the late developments'

explanation.surface: A former pupil has lately been dedicated to a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblate is a layperson dedicated to a religious community, historically a child given to a monastery.

clue.text: Dickensian simpleton involved in tedious donkey-work

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: dry means dull and tedious
Barnaby Rudge, the simple-minded hero of Dickens's novel

explanation.surface: A simple-minded Dickens character gets stuck with dull, laborious chores.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is hard, menial, monotonous labour, which is what donkey-work idiomatically means.

clue.text: Overt criminality that leaves us in the dark?

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for a blatant swindle done in plain view
second meaning, read literally: a theft of the light of day, which would leave everyone unable to see

explanation.walkthrough: The second meaning takes the idiom literally; the question mark flags that whimsical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a brazen rip-off committed openly, while the literal sense is stealing sunlight, which would bring darkness.

clue.text: Leader of union forcing rebellion

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter, so only the opening one is kept

blocks.note: first letter of union
prising means forcing open, as with a lever

explanation.surface: A trade union boss forces the workers into revolt.
explanation.definitionFit: An uprising is a popular revolt against authority, a synonym for rebellion.

clue.text: Old instrument found by a medic in Georgia

blocks.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
taken as written

explanation.surface: An antique instrument is discovered by a doctor in the US state of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the pieces are stacked: Georgia's abbreviation comes first, though the clue names it last.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamba is short for viola da gamba, the bowed string instrument of the Renaissance and Baroque.

clue.text: He delivers drinks possibly, meeting crew

blocks.note: a round of drinks is bought for a group; possibly flags it as one example
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A delivery man might be bringing drinks when he meets the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundsman is a tradesman, such as a milkman, who delivers goods along a regular route.

clue.text: Skilled workman arranging courses in building?

definitions.text: Skilled workman arranging courses in building?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone planning a set of lessons or menu courses
setter's reading: courses are the horizontal rows of a wall, laid during construction

explanation.surface: A tradesman seems to be organising classes or a meal in some building.
explanation.walkthrough: A course in masonry is one horizontal layer of bricks, so laying courses in a building is this trade's daily work.
explanation.definitionFit: This tradesman builds walls by setting bricks in mortar row upon row, each row being a course.

clue.text: Pout when ship runs out of creamy dessert

indicators.note: running out of something means leaving it, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: SS is steamship
a mousse is a light whipped pudding

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a sulky face when the vessel's galley has no more mousse.
explanation.definitionFit: A moue is a small pouting grimace of displeasure, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Robbers identified in simple song picked up at bar

indicators.note: picked up means heard or caught by the ear, so the word is taken by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: to bar is to ban
a ditty is a short simple song

explanation.surface: Bandits are spotted in a folk song heard at the pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: 'at bar' supplies the opening piece even though it is printed last.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti is the Italian-derived plural of bandit, meaning outlaws or brigands.

clue.text: Quiet chap serving alcoholic drink

blocks.note: sh is the call for quiet
a man's name, as chap often clues

explanation.surface: A softly spoken man works behind the bar pouring drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a weak but still alcoholic drink popular in Britain.

clue.text: Fashionable greeting used among Conservatives

indicators.note: used among a group means placed in its midst, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: C is Conservative; two of them make the plural
hi is a casual hello

explanation.surface: A trendy hello is going round among Tory party members.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish and elegant, the French word for being in fashion.

clue.text: Plant from east — a chap will be tedious about that

indicators.note: about means around, and that points back to the first item, so it is wrapped by the rest

blocks.note: he'll, short for he will
E is the compass abbreviation for east
to bore is to be tedious

explanation.surface: A gardener's warning that a man will be dull about a plant from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellebore is a flowering plant genus, including the Christmas rose.

clue.text: Generous with son in domestic situation

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the setting that follows

blocks.note: home is one's domestic setting
and means together with
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone is open-handed with their son at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome can mean large and liberal, as in a handsome tip or a handsome donation.

clue.text: Wine transforming nurse's tea

indicators.note: transforming means changing shape completely, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
taken as written

explanation.surface: Wine is turning the nurse's cup of tea into something stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauternes is a sweet white dessert wine from the Bordeaux region of France.

clue.text: Level-headed business manager initially worked as model

indicators.note: initially points to a word's beginning, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
first letter of manager
an artist's model poses

explanation.surface: A calm business manager once had a sideline as a model.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone composed is calm and in control of their feelings, which is what level-headed means.

clue.text: Take part in game with extremely eager theatre attender

indicators.note: extremely refers to the extremes of a word, so its two end letters are kept

blocks.note: to play is to take part
Go is the Japanese board game
first and last letters of eager

explanation.surface: A keen member of a theatre audience joins in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: A playgoer is someone who regularly attends the theatre.

clue.text: Woman securing Labrador's first bone

indicators.note: securing means holding tight, so the name grips the next piece inside it
first means only the opening letter of the word before it is wanted

blocks.note: a woman's name
first letter of Labrador

explanation.surface: A woman holds her Labrador's first bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the forearm.

clue.text: French writer left variable account supporting airline

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath, so the pieces named before it go below the piece named after it

blocks.note: BA is British Airways
L is the abbreviation for left
algebra uses x, y and z as variables
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: A French author has left a shifting account backing an airline.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, supporting means placed below, so the airline goes at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Honoré de Balzac was the 19th-century French novelist behind La Comédie humaine.

clue.text: Make fun of butt during first half of meal

indicators.note: during means within the span of, so one piece is placed inside the other
only the first half of the word is wanted, so its back half is dropped

blocks.note: supper is an evening meal
a butt is the end of something, like a cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the target of a joke midway through dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up is to parody or satirise someone, mocking them by imitation.

clue.text: How some may lie over goods held by party!

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it, so these pieces sit within the last one

blocks.note: a do is a party
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
G is good, so two of them make goods

explanation.surface: An exclamation about how some might stretch out over goods kept back for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: To lie doggo is a British idiom meaning to hide quietly and keep still.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb only occurs in the idiom 'lie doggo', so it describes the manner in which someone may lie low.

clue.text: Supporter church allowed wrist ornament

blocks.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
CE is the Church of England
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A churchgoing backer has permitted the wearing of jewellery.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracelet is a decorative band or chain worn around the wrist.

clue.text: Sly person loses head, finding support

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its top letter

blocks.note: a weasel is a sly, crafty person

explanation.surface: A cunning person is beheaded yet finds something to lean on.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand that supports a painter's canvas or a display board.

clue.text: Smell of game? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means half the word is left out, here its front half

blocks.note: ping-pong is table tennis

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a game smells, and the reply is an emphatic yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', which disguises the deletion.
explanation.definitionFit: Pong is British slang for a strong unpleasant smell, a stink.

clue.text: Initially such indolence brought about European corruption

indicators.note: initially points to a word's beginning, so only its opening letter is kept
brought about means taken around, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: first letter of such
indolence is laziness
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A claim that idleness led to corruption across Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleaziness is sordid, disreputable conduct, particularly the political kind called corruption.

clue.text: Support Liberal party at last: not to begin with

indicators.note: at last points to the end of the word, so only its final letter is used

blocks.note: to second a motion is to support it
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
last letter of party

explanation.surface: Backing for the Liberal party comes at last, though not at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Secondly introduces the second point of a list, so it is used where something is not first.

clue.text: Comfortable about first of these luxuries being expensive

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps what follows
first of points to the opening letters of the words after it

blocks.note: cosy means snug and comfortable
first letters of these and luxuries

explanation.surface: Comfortable surroundings with such luxuries are dear.
explanation.definitionFit: Costly means costing a lot, an everyday synonym for expensive.
